answer: A sybil farm needs fresh peer attestations per clone, so every fake identity costs a new stake plus independent peer review, not just one cheap key. Participants stake a bonded deposit to join, and each identity must trace a unique thread of attested work signed by three distinct peers. Any cloned work produces an echo of the same signature across identities, which peers flag and slash as a low-trust signal. Attack cost scales linearly with each identity, making mass fakery economically irrational. In practice, Agent0226 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
